ad: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: He was thirty-five in the year the Ka'ba was rebuilt. Even before revelation, Quraysh called him al-Amin, the trustworthy one.

yakinlik: His uncle
ozet: The wealthiest of the sons of Hashim. In a year of famine he took Ja'far into his care to lighten Abu Talib's burden. When the Ka'ba was rebuilt, he carried stones together with the Messenger of Allah.
When Quraysh hesitated to pull down the Ka'ba, he was the first to take up the pickaxe and begin.
A man of Quraysh who asked that only clean earnings go into the building of the Ka'ba.
The oldest man of Quraysh. In the dispute over the Black Stone, he proposed that the first person to enter through the gate of the sanctuary be the arbiter.

yakinlik: Grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: He reopened the well of Zamzam and took on the duty of providing water and food for the pilgrims; Quraysh sought his counsel. From time to time he withdrew to the cave on Hira to worship. In the Year of the Elephant he asked Abraha only for his camels: «I am the owner of the camels; the House, too, has an Owner who will protect it.»

yakinlik: Wife of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The daughter of Khuwaylid; a noble and wealthy lady of Quraysh who sent men to trade with her goods. Hearing of the Prophet's honesty, she offered him to take her goods to Syria; later she married him. She was the Prophet's first wife; all his children except Ibrahim were from her. In the years he worshipped alone at Hira, he took his provisions from her; from time to time Khadija went up to Hira with him.
He settled his wife Hagar and his son Ishmael in the valley of Mecca; together with his son he raised the foundations of the Ka'ba.
The son of Abraham. In Mecca he became kin to the people of Jurhum; together with his father he raised the foundations of the Ka'ba.
The wife of Abraham and the mother of Ishmael. She allowed the tribe of Jurhum to settle in Mecca.
Of the tribe of Khuza'a. When he took charge of Mecca and the Ka'ba, he spread idol worship.
He gathered Quraysh in Mecca, won the rule of Mecca and the Ka'ba for Quraysh, and built Dar al-Nadwa.

yakinlik: Father of 'Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's grandfather
ozet: With his brothers he made agreements with neighbouring states and with the tribes along the trade routes; thanks to this, the winter and summer trading journeys of Quraysh became safe.

yakinlik: The Prophet's cousin
ozet: The son of Abu Talib. In a year of famine his uncle al-'Abbas took him into his care. He described the Meccan society before Islam to the ruler of Abyssinia.

A man who gave up the worship of idols and sought the religion of Abraham. He became neither a Jew nor a Christian; he would not eat what was slaughtered in the name of idols, and he took in girls whom others wanted to kill. He died before the coming of prophethood.
One of the four men who turned away from idol worship to search for a religion. He took up Christianity and gained knowledge from the scriptures of the Jews and Christians.
One of the four men who turned away from idol worship to search for a religion; he remained undecided until he became a Muslim.
One of the four men who turned away from idol worship to search for a religion; he went to the Byzantine emperor and became a Christian.
The daughter of Abu Bakr. She told how she had seen the aged Zayd ibn 'Amr, his back against the Ka'ba, calling out to Quraysh.

The Abyssinian commander in Yemen, called 'al-Ashram' because of the wound on his face. He built a church in San'a and marched on Mecca with an elephant to destroy the Ka'ba; his army was scattered by the birds, and he died in San'a, where he returned wounded.
A nobleman of Yemen. He fought against Abraha, was defeated and taken prisoner. He was a friend of 'Abd al-Muttalib; while a prisoner he found someone to arrange his meeting with Abraha.
He resisted Abraha in the land of the Khath'am tribe, was defeated, and guided him. It is reported that he said into the elephant's ear: 'Kneel, Mahmud.'
In Ta'if he submitted to Abraha on behalf of Thaqif and gave him a man to show him the way.
The man Thaqif gave Abraha as a guide; he died at al-Mughammas, and the Arabs stoned his grave.
The envoy Abraha sent to Mecca, to 'Abd al-Muttalib.
Abraha's elephant keeper; he arranged 'Abd al-Muttalib's meeting with Abraha.

yakinlik: Father of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. His father had vowed to sacrifice one of his sons; the lot fell on 'Abdullah, and a hundred camels were sacrificed in his place. He married Amina; according to the preferred report, he died in Yathrib on his way back from Syria, before his son was born.

yakinlik: Mother of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The daughter of Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf, chief of the Banu Zuhra; she married 'Abdullah. When her son was born, she sent word to 'Abd al-Muttalib.

yakinlik: Maternal grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: Chief of the Banu Zuhra branch of Quraysh; he married his daughter Amina to 'Abdullah.

yakinlik: Wet nurse of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: Of the Sa'd ibn Bakr branch of the Hawazin tribe. In a year of famine she came to Mecca and took the Prophet, whom no one else would take because he was an orphan, as her nursling; she raised him until he was four or five.

yakinlik: Foster father of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: Halima's husband. He agreed to their taking the Prophet, saying: 'Perhaps Allah will give us a blessing through him.'
A servant of Abu Lahab; she nursed the Prophet for a while after his birth.
According to the authentic report, while the Prophet was with his wet nurse, Gabriel opened his chest and washed his heart with Zamzam water.

yakinlik: The Prophet's nurse
ozet: Of Abyssinian origin. She went with Amina on the journey to Yathrib; when Amina died at al-Abwa, she brought the Prophet to Mecca and handed him over to his grandfather. The Messenger of Allah would say of her: 'She is my mother after my mother.'

yakinlik: Uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. He and the Prophet's father 'Abdullah shared both mother and father. Before he died, his father had entrusted his grandson to him; he took his eight-year-old nephew in and raised him. He was respected among Quraysh and his word carried weight; his family was large. He loved his nephew dearly, believed he brought good fortune, and kept him with him even on his journeys; he took him on the journey to Syria when he was twelve. In a year of famine, to lighten his burden, the Prophet took his son 'Ali and al-'Abbas took Ja'far.

A monk who lived in his monastery at Busra. According to a report, he saw the twelve-year-old Prophet in the Quraysh caravan that came with his uncle, recognised the signs of prophethood, and told Abu Talib to protect him. The soundness of this report is disputed among scholars.

yakinlik: Wife of Abu Talib, aunt of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: While the Prophet was growing up with his uncle Abu Talib, she cared for him even more than for her own children.

yakinlik: Uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. In the fourth Fijar war he commanded the sons of Hashim. After a merchant of Zubayd was wronged, he persuaded 'Abdullah ibn Jud'an and led the way to the Hilf al-Fudul pact.

Chief of the Banu Taym, one of the richest, oldest and most influential men of Mecca. He insisted that the sons of Hashim also take part in the Fijar war; the Hilf al-Fudul pact was made in his house.
Commander-in-chief of Quraysh and Kinana in the fourth Fijar war.
One of the notables of Quraysh. According to most reports, he did not pay a merchant of Zubayd for the goods he had bought; this incident is reported to have led to the Hilf al-Fudul pact.
Of the tribe of Kinana. He killed 'Urwa al-Rahhal, who was protecting the caravan of the ruler of al-Hira, in a sacred month; this is what started the fourth Fijar war.
Of the Hawazin tribe. While protecting the caravan of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, ruler of al-Hira, he was killed by Barrad ibn Qays in a sacred month.

yakinlik: Khadija's servant
ozet: Khadija's servant. He was with the Prophet on the trading journey he made to Syria with Khadija's goods.

yakinlik: Uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The son of 'Abd al-Muttalib. According to Ibn Hisham's report, he went with the Prophet to ask for Khadija's hand from her father Khuwaylid.

yakinlik: Son of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: The first child of the Prophet and Khadija. The Prophet took the name 'Abu al-Qasim' from him. He died young.

yakinlik: Adopted son of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
ozet: Of the Kalb tribe. As a child he was kidnapped and sold as a slave; Khadija gave him to the Prophet. When his father came to take him, he chose to stay with the Prophet; the Prophet freed him and adopted him.

yakinlik: Khadija's nephew
ozet: Khadija's nephew. From among the slaves he brought, Khadija chose Zayd ibn Haritha.

yakinlik: Father of Zayd ibn Haritha
ozet: The father of Zayd ibn Haritha. He searched for his kidnapped son for years and at last came to Mecca; Zayd chose to stay with the Prophet.

yakinlik: The Prophet's cousin
ozet: The son of Abu Talib. In a year of famine in Mecca, the Prophet took him in to lighten his uncle's burden; 'Ali stayed with the Prophet until he became a prophet.
